summary:
TerraLoop is an open-source, trilingual (English, Hindi, Punjabi) crop rotation decision-support platform built with NASA Earth Observations, biophysical simulation, and multi-objective optimization.

Addressing shifting temperatures, erratic rainfall, groundwater depletion, stubble burning, and soil degradation, TerraLoop integrates NASA POWER, GPM IMERG, SMAP L4, GRACE-FO, NASADEM, FIRMS, HLS 30m, and NEX-GDDP-CMIP6 with SoilGrids 2.0, ESA WorldCereal, Meteomatics 90m hydrology, and local Soil Health Card inputs. Its FAO-56 water-thermal, RothC soil carbon, RUSLE erosion, and 6-objective NSGA-II models let farmers weight profit, water savings, soil health, drought risk, labour, and nutrition across 40 crops and CMIP6 climate futures.

Static crop calendars lock farmers into vulnerable monocultures. In Sangrur, Punjab, where GRACE measures -4.15 cm/yr aquifer loss, shifting from puddled rice-wheat to TerraLoop's top rotations cuts irrigation 17.6% to 60.1%, expands sowing windows from 11 to 26–34 burn-free days, builds up to +3.29 t C/ha soil carbon over 10 years, and raises median profit from ₹170,334 to ₹271,978/ha—validated across 11 benchmarks on six continents (13.0% held-out MAPE).
details:
What Does It Do & How Does It Work?

TerraLoop is an open-science crop-rotation decision-support platform that turns NASA Earth observations, local soil properties, and farmer priorities into ranked 1–3 year crop rotations, seasonal calendars, and financial/climate risk forecasts for any field worldwide. The code can be found at - https://github.com/Anshsurana123/nasa-farm-hackathon

  1. Field Profiling (profiler.py): Given a coordinate, map polygon, or address/Google Maps link, TerraLoop runs a 12-future parallel pipeline fusing NASA satellite streams—POWER, GPM IMERG V07 (rainfall), SMAP L4 (root-zone moisture), GRACE/GRACE-FO (aquifer trends), NASADEM (slope/aspect), FIRMS (active crop-residue fires), HLS L30/S30 (30 m NDVI phenology via Savitzky–Golay smoothing & Gaussian ML classification), NEX-GDDP-CMIP6 (SSP2-4.5 & SSP5-8.5 for 2030s/2050s), and GIBS WMTS context layers—alongside ISRIC SoilGrids 2.0 (250 m), ESA WorldCereal 10 m, Köppen-Geiger agro-ecological zones, and Meteomatics 90 m weather/hydrology/agro-hazards. Farmers can override satellite soil estimates with lab values from a Government Soil Health Card (SHC) (pH, SOC %, N, P, K).
  2. Coupled Biophysical & Economic Simulation (models/): Rather than guessing yields, TerraLoop simulates daily water balance, heat stress, and long-term field health across 30-year historical moving weather blocks or CMIP6 climate ensembles using deterministic physics models: FAO-56 Penman–Monteith ET0ET_0ET0​ (with Hargreaves fallback and Ambika–Mishra MERRA-2 irrigated cooling bias correction), Saxton–Rawls (2006) soil hydraulics, FAO-56 / FAO-33 daily water & March terminal heat balance, RothC-26.3 10-year 5-pool soil organic carbon + legume biological nitrogen fixation (N balance), kinetic RUSLE (EI30EI_{30}EI30​) soil erosion, regional enterprise crop budgets (P10/P50/P90P_{10}/P_{50}/P_{90}P10​/P50​/P90​ + CVaR10CVaR_{10}CVaR10​ drought-tail risk), and ICMR-NIN / USDA FoodData Central caloric & protein nutrition.
  3. Multi-Objective Optimization (optimize/): Candidate rotations across 40 crops (packages/crop-kb/) are screened via crop/soil/water suitability rules (and a degree-2 Polynomial Ridge surrogate when candidates exceed 85), then ranked by a 6-objective NSGA-II Pareto optimizer (Profit, Water Savings weighted dynamically up to 1.50× by GRACE aquifer decline, Soil Health, Low Drought Risk CVaR10CVaR_{10}CVaR10​, Low Labour, and Food Security).

What Benefits Does It Have?

  • Translates Science Into Farmer Language: Converts technical outputs into practical numbers farmers actually use: borewell pumping hours saved, 75 mm irrigations saved, 45-kg Urea bags saved/ha, burn-free harvest-to-sowing turnaround days, income in a severe drought year (CVaR10CVaR_{10}CVaR10​), and a 1-click /Acre (Killa) vs /Ha unit toggle.
  • Trilingual & Low-Bandwidth Accessible: Full English, Hindi (हिन्दी), and Punjabi (ਪੰਜਾਬੀ) support (780 synchronized UI keys) plus printable KVK/agronomic briefs and automatic matching against 26 Indian Central/State & global conservation schemes (e.g., PM-PRANAM, Mera Pani Meri Virasat, SMAM, USDA EQIP/CSP, EU CAP Eco-Schemes, Brazil Plano ABC+, Kenya KCSAP, Australia ACCU).
  • Farmer Priorities Truly Control Outcomes: Verified by a 200-vector monotonicity test (0 violations), ensuring shifts in user priorities measurably steer rotation rankings while allowing users to lock must-grow crops, exclude crops, toggle livestock fodder, or stress-test rotations under custom drought, harvest-price, and fertilizer shocks.

What Is the Intended Impact?

TerraLoop aims to replace static, unsustainable monocultures with resilient rotations that protect groundwater, soil carbon, air quality, and farm income:

  • Hero Transformation (Sangrur, Punjab, precomputed engine output): Replacing Puddled Rice → Wheat → Fallow (1,128.6 mm/yr median irrigation, 11-day burn crunch, -1.92 t C/ha 10-yr SOC loss, ₹170,334/ha P50P_{50}P50​ profit, ₹77,208/ha CVaR10CVaR_{10}CVaR10​):
    • Rank #1 (DSR Rice → Sunflower → Mung bean): Cuts irrigation 17.6% (113 pump hrs/ha saved), widens the harvest window to 26 burn-free days, flips 10-yr soil carbon to +3.01 t C/ha (Soil Health 87.7/100), saves 3.5 Urea bags/ha, raises median profit ~60% (₹271,978/ha), and nearly triples drought-year income (₹217,384/ha CVaR10CVaR_{10}CVaR10​).
    • Rank #2 (Maize → Sunflower → Mung bean): Cuts irrigation 60.1% (386 pump hrs/ha saved), opens a 34-day zero-till window, builds +3.29 t C/ha SOC, saves 3.5 Urea bags/ha, and still lifts median profit ~35% (₹230,542/ha).
  • Global Scalability: Empirically checked across 6 Indian benchmark districts and 5 global breadbasket hubs on 6 continents (13.0% MAPE across 14 held-out rainfed crop-hub pairs in Ames USA, Chartres France, Sorriso Brazil, Nakuru Kenya, and Wagga Wagga Australia).

Tools, Coding Languages, Hardware & Software Used

  • Backend & Science Engine: Python 3.11+, FastAPI (>=0.111), Uvicorn, Pydantic v2 (>=2.6), NumPy (>=1.26), pandas (>=2.2), PyYAML, httpx, earthengine-api, and google-auth, managed with uv workspaces (terraloop-schemas, terraloop-engine, terraloop-api).
  • Frontend & Geospatial UI: TypeScript, Next.js 16.3, React 19.2, Tailwind CSS v4, MapLibre GL JS 6.12, Lucide React, and custom HTML5 Canvas stratigraphy (SoilColumn3D).
  • Earth Observation & Ancillary APIs: Google Earth Engine, NASA POWER, NASA GPM IMERG V07, NASA SMAP L4, NASA GRACE/GRACE-FO, NASADEM, NASA FIRMS, NASA HLS L30/S30, NASA NEX-GDDP-CMIP6, NASA GIBS WMTS, Meteomatics 90 m API, ISRIC SoilGrids 2.0, ESA WorldCereal 10 m, Natural Earth, and Nominatim/OSM.
  • DevOps, Testing & Design Tools: pytest (124 passing offline tests), Ruff, ESLint, GitHub Actions CI (including deterministic git diff --exit-code docs/BENCHMARKS.md verification), Docker, Vercel (vercel.json multi-service config), Canva, and PowerPoint (developed and tested on standard developer laptops/workstations running Windows/Linux—requiring zero specialized GPU hardware).

How Is Your Project Creative?

  1. Physics First, Zero Black-Box Yield Hallucination: Instead of asking an LLM to invent crop advice, every yield, carbon, water, and income number comes from cited pure-Python biophysical equations; optional Gemini narrative summaries are gated by a 5% numeric grounding verifier (verify_llm_numeric_grounding) that rejects ungrounded numbers.
  2. A 3-Tier Global Honesty Gate (validated_india / validated_regional / biophysical_global): Rather than extrapolating regional crop prices into uncalibrated countries, coordinates outside calibrated economic hubs automatically zero out proxy financial weights (allow_economic_ranking=False) so rankings depend strictly on water, soil health, and nutrition physics—paired with transparent scope banners.
  3. Connecting Space Telemetry to Everyday Farm Decisions: Coupling orbital GRACE groundwater overdraft directly to optimization weights, HLS/FIRMS burn windows to turnaround days, and Happy Seeder residue mulch to -1.0°C wheat terminal heat buffering turns macro Earth observation into hyper-local action.

What Factors Did Our Team Consider?

  • Data Provenance & Graceful Offline Resilience: Every value carries provenance (observed vs hybrid_regional vs demo_snapshot), disk caching protects against external API rate limits, urban SoilGrids mask gaps trigger up to a 3 km agricultural neighborhood search, and missing satellite feeds never fabricate synthetic observations.
  • Climate Bias & Calibration Discipline: We explicitly corrected MERRA-2's irrigated cooling bias across the Indo-Gangetic Plain (-4.5°C in March per Ambika & Mishra 2019), separated calibration (Sangrur) from held-out evaluation districts (Ludhiana, Bathinda, Thanjavur, Yavatmal, Jhansi, and 5 global hubs), and transparently disclosed unmodeled biotic gaps (e.g., rainfed cotton bollworm in peninsular India).
  • Real Farmer Equity & Downside Risk: Farmers care most about surviving bad years—so we optimized CVaR10CVaR_{10}CVaR10​ tail income alongside median profit, modeled MSP/NAFED market-risk tiers and North/South Hemisphere sowing calendars, and delivered the entire interface in regional languages and local land units (/Acre (Killa)).
